method: each configuration measured in a FRESH process (scripts/measure_one.py). DirectML's allocator grows its heap and never shrinks it within a process, so measuring several configs in one interpreter contaminates every result after the first.
key_finding: The binding tensor is the vocabulary projection: batch*seq*vocab*4 bytes, which at 32768 tokens dominates every other allocation. 2*512*32768*4 = 128 MiB per copy and roughly 384 MiB with the fp32 softmax and backward; 2*1024*32768*4 = 256 MiB per copy and ~768 MiB with softmax, which is what the OOM messages report.
corrections: Earlier claim 'usable VRAM is 3.62 GiB' was wrong: that is the single-allocation cap. 10.00 GiB is reachable across many tensors.

Earlier OOM results for 117m at b=1 seq=2048 and b=2 seq=1024 were partly a harness artefact (memory not released between trials). Re-measured in fresh processes: those two still OOM, but for a different and now-understood reason -- the logits tensor.
Earlier attribution of the shortfall to the display compositor was wrong: only 1.11 GiB is in use, and closing Opera would free 0.50 GiB of it, which changes nothing.
verdict: mini (244,354,048 params) trains at 391 tok/s at b=2 seq=512. 117m trains at 838 tok/s at b=2 seq=512. small (705M) OOMs.
